column1: # Invented names written blind, in the shares one meets on profiles of
# self-employed people in NRW, by someone who had not seen the rules:
# the name, the part of the profile's link after /in/, the first name a
# careful person greets them by, and ? for the family name, which this
# set does not ask. Lines starting with "# miss" are read wrong today,
# Realistic held-out set of LinkedIn display names of self-employed people in NRW,
# with profile handle and the first name a careful German writer would greet them by.
# All names are invented. Columns: name, handle, expected first name (empty = cannot tell).
#   ~55% plain "First Last" (about 2/3 German, 1/3 Turkish, Arabic, Kurdish, Polish, Russian,
#        Ukrainian, Italian, Greek, Balkan, Spanish, Portuguese, Dutch, Persian, Vietnamese,
#   ~7% academic or professional title before the name (Dr., Dr. med., Prof., Dipl.-Ing., Mag., RA, StB)
#   ~5% credentials or job title after the name (MBA, M.Sc., LL.M., PCC, Dipl.-Psych.)
#   ~7% double first names (hyphenated or not) and middle names or initials
#   ~3% particles (von, van der, de, Di, ter, zur, Freifrau von)
#   ~2% nickname shown next to the name
#   ~3% all caps or all lowercase, ~1.5% styled Unicode letters
#   ~2% family name first (Asian order, SURNAME Given, Surname, Given)
#   ~1.5% role word before the name (Coach, Fotografin, Rechtsanwalt, Heilpraktikerin)
#   ~2.5% initials or a single name, ~1% a business name instead of a person
#   ~2% double family names or maiden names
# Handles: ~70% generated first-last plus a random suffix, ~17% plain first-last or
#   firstlast, ~13% custom (coach-sabine, ra-kortmann, ...-coaching, dr-...). Umlauts kept,
#   written ae/oe/ue, or dropped. Overlapping features (title plus tagline) count once.
